text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
BURSA
- Shares in Romanian car maker Dacia Automobile will be traded on the stock exchange within the next three weeks, the newspaper says.
- Swiss farmers are leasing agricultural land in the southern Dolj county, the newspaper says.
- The finance ministry will make a T-bills offer on August 19, to raise 1.13 trillion lei in one-year bills to refinance the state budget, the newspaper says.

- The manager of Rocar SA bus maker, which won a tender to supply 300 buses to the Bucharest city hall in 1997-1998, says in an interview that access to credits is among major problems facing the company.
ADEVARUL
- Following negotiations with the trade unions, the government has set wage indexations at 15 percent starting August, and at 14 percent starting October, the newspaper says.
ROMANIA
- The newspaper quotes an opinion survey as showing that 55 percent of Romanians believe that the reform steps taken by the government will yield good results.
- The State Ownership Fund has agreed on a programme to restructure Brasov-based truck maker Roman Sa, by laying off some 3,000 employees and breaking the plant into smaller units.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The price of sugar produced in Romania exceeds costs, the newspaper quotes Constanta Savin, manager of a sugar factory in Calarasi, as saying. Cheap sugar imported from Ukraine via Moldova, has swamped the Romanian market, Savin said.
General:
LIBERTATEA
- National Peasant Party leaders have decided to shelve, for the time being, their plans to change the law on houses nationalised by the communists, the newspaper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper runs a report on recent landslides which hit a village in the Prahova county, north of Bucharest, after heavy rains over the past few weeks.
- A Canadian woman, aged 116, has dethroned Romanian Anitica Butariu as the oldest living human, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Romania on September 18, as part of a tour of central and eastern Europe, the newspaper says.
- Deputy Education Minister Florin Diaconescu has tendered his resignation over disputes with senior ministry officials, the newspaper says.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264 REUTER
